item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
Darin asked his friends to name their favorite color. He collected the information in the table shown below.

| Favorite Color | Number of Friends |
| --- | --- |
| Red | 4 |
| Green | 2 |
| Blue | 6 |
| Yellow | 7 |

Then Darin started to draw a graph to show the information. Complete Darin’s graph.

[Image: Bar graph with title Favorite color, x-axis labeled Color, y-axis labeled Number of friends. Two columns labeled Red and Green are shown.]

descriptors: Both bars drawn correctly: blue to 6, yellow to 7 (± 0.5)
One or both bars attempted but not correct
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

item.figure_description: An incomplete vertical bar graph titled "Favorite Color". The vertical axis on the left is labeled "Number of Friends" with tick marks and horizontal grid lines at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The horizontal axis at the bottom is labeled "Color" and has four equally spaced categories separated by tick marks, labeled from left to right: "Red", "Green", "Blue", and "Yellow". A gray bar of height 4 is drawn above "Red". A gray bar of height 2 is drawn above "Green". The spaces above "Blue" and "Yellow" are empty.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.
